# Research
[bold]Unlike typical Space Station science, research within the SCP Foundation is based primarily on SCP objects.[/bold] Here, researching all technologies requires [color=#8b0000]SCP Research Points[/color], which can be obtained by unlocking SCP nodes — utilizing a system similar to the artifact system — or through unique interactions.
## The Artifact System Process
To begin, the SCP object must be located within a radius of 10 tiles from the Analysis Platform. Unlike standard artifacts, it is not strictly necessary for the object to be positioned directly *on* the platform. This functionality applies exclusively to [color=#2B662B]living SCPs[/color]—such as SCP-173, etc.
As soon as the effect is triggered, [color=#8b0000]the corresponding SCP Research Points will be instantly credited to the server[/color]. There is no need to manually extract them via the console.
Subsequent research proceeds in the standard manner, with the sole exception that the visual effect of the trigger will remain hidden.
[italic]We have expanded the standard list of effects, so you will be able to discover entirely new effects that objects can manifest. Some of them are incredibly wild.[/italic]
## A Path Through Unique Interactions
Some SCPs feature their own unique interactions, yet they all operate according to a single underlying mechanism:
- The player interacts with the SCP using the required tool. - After a brief waiting period, the player receives [bold]research material[/bold]. - The SCP enters a cooldown phase, the duration of which depends on the specific interaction performed. Further interactions are impossible until this cooldown expires—even if they involve different types of interactions.
The resulting [bold]research material[/bold] can be studied like a regular artifact. Each node provides significantly [color=#8b0000]more SCP research points[/color] than SCP item nodes.
